model_output.summary: At Harrod and Blake, you run the front office for a six-attorney firm while handling billing and trust account reconciliation. Earlier work in a two-dentist practice adds patient scheduling, insurance claims, and front desk training. Together, the roles support an office manager reading, with responsibility across people, calendars, and financial administration. The resume doesn't yet explain how you handled exceptions in the trust reconciliation, which would help a reviewer understand that part of the job.
strengths: Roughly 90 client invoices a month gives a useful sense of the billing workload.
Hiring and supervising two receptionists makes your staff responsibility clear.
The dentistry role names about 40 patients a day and training for three new front desk staff, giving context to both service and training work.
gaps: The software transition doesn't explain your part in introducing the system, so the implementation work is difficult to distinguish from routine use.
Vendor contract work doesn't say whether you selected providers, negotiated terms, or handled another part of the process.
The current role is packed into one paragraph, making court deadlines, reconciliation, and staff supervision harder to scan separately.
